title: How Doctors Smash a Kidney Stone Without Cutting You
sources: Shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL): shock waves aimed from outside the body break kidney/ureteric stones into small pieces that are passed in urine; usually thousands of shocks per session (NHS, 'Kidney stones - Treatment'; NIDDK, 'Treatment for Kidney Stones')
Kidney stones can block the ureter (the tube draining the kidney) and cause severe pain (renal colic) (NHS; NIDDK)

Roller coaster study: Mitchell & Wartinger (2016), J Am Osteopath Assoc 116(10):647-652 - a 3D-printed model kidney with real stones ridden on a roller coaster; small stones passed far more often, especially in the back seat

lines.text: This kidney stone is stuck, and the pain is brutal. Here's how doctors smash it without a single cut.
It's jammed in the tube that drains your kidney.
So doctors fire thousands of shock waves at it, from outside your body.
Each wave cracks it a little more,
until it shatters into tiny grains, like sand.
Then you just pee the pieces out.
And here's the twist. In a model kidney, riding a roller coaster helped small stones pass.
Would you ride one to skip the pain? Tell me below.
